_comment: Octail's own egg (no upstream file; pelican-eggs' games-standalone minetest egg was read as a reference only). Luanti publishes no Linux server build of its own (only Windows, macOS and Android), so the install takes Alpine 3.22's luanti-server package and its libraries with apk, which checks them against Alpine's signed index, into luanti/ (the C library comes from the runtime image, also Alpine 3.22), and the chosen game from ContentDB, pinned with a SHA-256 recorded in the script since ContentDB publishes none: Minetest Game or VoxeLibre, or any game the owner uploads into games/. The server runs with MINETEST_USER_PATH at the server folder, so worlds/, mods/, games/ and minetest.conf are where the file manager shows them; the game is passed with --gameid only while the world doesn't exist yet (Luanti would otherwise run the world with another game). minetest.conf is written once by the install and edited with the properties parser before every start. The dedicated server reads no console input (--terminal is a full-screen ncurses console); it saves and stops on Ctrl+C.
name: Luanti
author: eggs@octail.net
description: Luanti (formerly Minetest) is a free, open-source voxel game engine: build, mine and explore in Minetest Game, VoxeLibre or any game from ContentDB, with thousands of mods.
startup: [ -x ./luanti/usr/bin/luantiserver ] || { echo "Luanti is not installed: reinstall the server."; exit 1; }; export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(pwd)/luanti/usr/lib" MINETEST_USER_PATH="$(pwd)"; case "${LUANTI_GAME}" in voxelibre) LUANTI_ID=mineclone2 ;; *) LUANTI_ID="${LUANTI_GAME}" ;; esac; exec ./luanti/usr/bin/luantiserver --port {{SERVER_PORT}} --config minetest.conf --world "worlds/{{WORLD_NAME}}" $( [ -f "worlds/${WORLD_NAME}/world.mt" ] || printf -- '--gameid %s' "${LUANTI_ID}" )

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Luanti (formerly Minetest) installation script (Octail): Alpine's signed luanti-server package and the libraries it
# needs, installed with apk into /mnt/server/luanti (apk checks every package against Alpine's signed index), since
# the game container can't install packages, and the chosen game from ContentDB, pinned and checked by SHA-256.
# The runtime image is Alpine 3.22 like this installer, so the libraries match; the C library always comes from the
# image. Failures exit non-zero.
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
set -euo pipefail

## The games offered by name, pinned: ContentDB publishes no checksums, so each release's SHA-256 is recorded here.
## To update: pick the release on https://content.luanti.org/api/packages/<author>/<name>/releases/ (its
## min_minetest_version must be at most the Luanti version Alpine ships), download its zip, put its url and sha256sum
## here.
MTG_URL=https://cdn.content.luanti.org/uploads/c1c185d0c4.zip # Minetest Game 2026-08-17
MTG_SHA256=5b364f6b0cf31ec336319492e14106d932eb86b65a91ded99f4b25f4876519dc
VL_URL=https://cdn.content.luanti.org/uploads/6b12075e71.zip # VoxeLibre 0.92.3
VL_SHA256=51ea9242aabb1f29575abbfb599c79bcde9435616ea097c0582e11ac1b2b279d

cd /mnt/server
ALPINE=$(cut -d. -f1,2 /etc/alpine-release)

## Luanti and its libraries into luanti/ (the program only: worlds, mods, games and minetest.conf stay on a reinstall)
rm -rf /mnt/server/luanti
if ! apk add --quiet --root /mnt/server/luanti --initdb --no-scripts --no-cache \
    --keys-dir /etc/apk/keys --repositories-file /etc/apk/repositories luanti-server; then
    echo "Installation failed: apk couldn't install luanti-server from Alpine ${ALPINE}."
    exit 1
fi
VERSION=$(apk info --root /mnt/server/luanti -e -v luanti-server 2>/dev/null || true)
## the C library comes from the image (the same Alpine release): never a second copy
rm -f /mnt/server/luanti/lib/ld-musl-* /mnt/server/luanti/lib/libc.musl-*
## Alpine still names the program minetestserver; Luanti's own name is luantiserver
if [ ! -e /mnt/server/luanti/usr/bin/luantiserver ] && [ -x /mnt/server/luanti/usr/bin/minetestserver ]; then
    ln -s minetestserver /mnt/server/luanti/usr/bin/luantiserver
fi
if [ ! -x /mnt/server/luanti/usr/bin/luantiserver ] || [ ! -d /mnt/server/luanti/usr/share/luanti/builtin ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: the Luanti server is missing after installing luanti-server."
    exit 1
fi

## the chosen game: downloaded, checked, and unpacked over an older copy of the same game
install_game() { # <url> <sha256> <folder> <title>
    echo "Downloading $4 from $1"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o /tmp/game.zip "$1"; then
        echo "Installation failed: $4 couldn't be downloaded."
        exit 1
    fi
    if ! echo "$2  /tmp/game.zip" | sha256sum -c --quiet -; then
        rm -f /tmp/game.zip
        echo "Installation failed: the $4 download doesn't match its checksum."
        exit 1
    fi
    rm -rf "games/$3"
    unzip -q -o /tmp/game.zip -d games
    rm -f /tmp/game.zip
    if [ ! -f "games/$3/game.conf" ]; then
        echo "Installation failed: $4 is missing after unpacking."
        exit 1
    fi
}
mkdir -p games mods worlds
case "${LUANTI_GAME:-minetest_game}" in
    minetest_game) install_game "$MTG_URL" "$MTG_SHA256" minetest_game "Minetest Game" ;;
    voxelibre) install_game "$VL_URL" "$VL_SHA256" mineclone2 "VoxeLibre" ;;
    *) echo "Game ${LUANTI_GAME}: not downloaded; upload it into games/ (its folder name is the game id)." ;;
esac

## a minimal minetest.conf, only when there is none; Octail sets the port, name, description, slots, listing, admin and
## game mode before every start
if [ ! -f minetest.conf ]; then
    cat > minetest.conf <<'EOF'
# Luanti server settings: https://docs.luanti.org/for-server-hosts/ (every setting: luanti/usr/share/luanti/builtin/settingtypes.txt).
# Octail sets port, server_name, server_description, motd, max_users, server_announce, name, creative_mode and
# enable_damage before every start (Startup tab); the other settings are yours.
port = 30000
server_name = Luanti Server
server_description =
motd =
max_users = 15
server_announce = false
name =
creative_mode = false
enable_damage = true
EOF
fi

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed: ${VERSION:-Luanti} (Alpine ${ALPINE}), game ${LUANTI_GAME:-minetest_game}."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Game
variables.description: The game a new world is created with: minetest_game (Minetest Game) or voxelibre (VoxeLibre), both downloaded by the install, or the id (folder name) of a game you upload into games/. An existing world keeps its game. Reinstall after switching to minetest_game or voxelibre.

variables.name: World Name
variables.description: The world folder in worlds/ (letters, digits, _ and -). A new name starts a new world.

variables.name: Server Name
variables.description: The name in the public server list (up to 64 characters, no double quotes or backslashes).

variables.name: Server Description
variables.description: Optional: the description in the public server list (no double quotes or backslashes).

variables.name: Message of the Day
variables.description: Optional: shown to players when they join (no double quotes or backslashes).

variables.name: Max Players
variables.description: How many players may be online at once (1-200).

variables.name: Public Server List
variables.description: true lists the server on servers.luanti.org; false keeps it off the list (players join by address).

variables.name: Admin Player
variables.description: Optional: the player name that gets every privilege on this server (up to 20 letters, digits, _ or -). Register that name first, or anyone who joins with it becomes admin.

variables.name: Creative Mode
variables.description: true gives everyone unlimited blocks (for games that support it, such as Minetest Game).

variables.name: Damage
variables.description: false makes players unable to take damage or die.
